stem: Under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), a manifestation determination review must be held in all children with:

options.text: Absence of other indications of anxiety in the child

stem: The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study® gathered data on over 11,000 children aged nine to ten across the United States, and asked parents to report whether their children experienced school detention or suspension in the past year. A nine-year-old with oppositional defiant disorder (ODD) is eligible to participate in a research study designed to assess the efficacy of a parenting intervention for ODD. stem: A school age child spends four hours per day arranging their room in an exact way and becomes highly distressed if items are moved around or appear "off" in the room. options.text: time required to perform the service.
insurance to be billed for the service.

stem: The parents of a 14-year-old report that their teen has discussed frequently switching sexual orientation, with occasional comments about being pansexual. options.text: "Such conflicts are common and reflect that the adolescent is likely to identify as homosexual as an adult."

stem: A clinician is consulted to see a school-age child for emotional outbursts. options.text: Development of tolerance to the fluvoxamine

stem: Which cell type provides scaffolding for the migration of neurons during prenatal neurogenesis?
A 15-year-old patient was discharged from a psychiatric practice a year ago to primary care. Which of the following responsibilities persist for the psychiatrist?
At the onset of a forensic evaluation, which of the following warnings should the clinician review with the youth and family?

options.text: Their role is to relieve the suffering of their client.
There is limited confidentiality with this type of evaluation.
The session is required to be both video and audio recorded.
Their sole purpose is to confirm a diagnosis and treatment plan.
The evaluation will be based solely on their report from this session.

stem: A previously healthy adolescent presents with fatigue, bilateral lower extremity weakness, and unilateral loss of vision. A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan with contrast demonstrates white matter hyperintense lesions in the optic tract and periventricular regions of the brain. Which of the following diagnoses best describes this patient's condition?
Adolescents and young adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) differ from their typically developing age peers in:

options.text: interest in having a romantic partner.
rate of identification with birth gender.
interest in increasing knowledge about sexuality.

stem: A psychiatrist volunteers at a free clinic in an attempt to prevent antipsychotic medications being prescribed to socioeconomically vulnerable children. This behavior most closely reflects which of the following ethical principles?

A psychiatrist asks their patient a reflective, open-ended question regarding the patient's desire to regain a healthy weight, despite repeated use of diuretics with its negative consequences. This is most likely an example of which therapeutic strategy?

A patient with very early onset schizophrenia presents with new onset waxy flexibility, echopraxia and echolalia, and has an extremely poor dietary and fluid intake. Primary neurological etiologies have been ruled out. There was very poor response to benzodiazepines and atypical antipsychotics. Which of the following is the next course of action?

A 16-year-old has been stable on 200 mg of clozapine for several months. A complete blood count is ordered with results as follows: WBC = 3100/ul; ANC = 1300/ul. The youth has no fever, swollen lymph nodes, or other signs of infection. What would be the best action to take in addition to getting a hematology consult?

options.text: Continue clozapine and monitor three times a week
Discontinue clozapine and monitor three times a week

stem: A 15-year-old previously healthy female presents with altered mental status and severe agitation. She slowly developed progressive confusion and memory deficits three weeks ago, with no clear trigger. Over the past two weeks, she has experienced hallucinations, poor sleep, and inattention. Prior to the visit she had a witnessed brief seizure episode. On assessment, she exhibits significant tachycardia and hypertension with an otherwise normal physical exam. Her preliminary ultrasound shows an ovarian lesion. Which of the following diagnoses is most likely consistent with this presentation?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department (ED) by her parents for odd behavior. Medical history is significant for asthma and allergic rhinitis. She was recently started on aripiprazole, and her parents state that she has been acting differently since then, being more irritable and active. The girl reports feeling restless, anxious, and uncomfortable. On examination, she is notably irritable and is pacing back and forth next to her bed in the ED. The remainder of the examination is normal. What is the next best step in management of the child?

A 17-year-old patient is referred for a psychiatric evaluation after multiple appointments with their primary physician for various medical complaints. The patient reports occasional mild chest pain and is constantly anxious about when the next pain might appear. The patient is also spending hours each night reading about causes of chest pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old gets into a physical fight with a fellow student who is always taunting and teasing others. According to the acute threat response system theory of impulsive aggression, which of the following brain regions modulates the aggression response by analyzing the costs of benefits of actions?
Which of the following interventions is classified as universal prevention?

options.text: Psychological First Aid: Listen, Protect, and Connect
Cognitive-Behavioral Interventions for Trauma in Schools

stem: A child with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus presents with five days of lethargy, confusion, and affective changes. Over the past three days, the child has not been eating, drinking, talking, or sleeping and has been maintaining odd postures. Symptoms do not change throughout the day. Use of lorazepam improves the patient's mentation and functioning. Which of the following diagnoses best describes the child's psychiatric comorbidity?
Which of the following psychological tests is often utilized to assess visuomotor integration in youth?
Which of the following signs or symptoms discriminates a primary psychotic disorder from the psychotic-like phenomena experienced secondary to trauma?

A four-year-old presents with dizziness, unsteady gait, and sudden, brief episodes of losing balance. The family reports that the child's eyes dart back and forth, but there is no loss of consciousness. Symptoms last one to two minutes and then subside spontaneously. This child is most at risk for developing what other neurological condition?

An adolescent who moved to the United States as a child from El Salvador speaks English fluently with their many American friends. During soccer season, the adolescent's family throws parties attended by friends from both El Salvador and America. The adolescent particularly loves serving pupusas and speaking Spanish at the parties. Which of the following strategies of acculturation is most likely to have been adopted by the adolescent?

An adolescent with longstanding chronic fatigue reports periods of falling asleep suddenly in school. The adolescent is fearful, reporting not being able to move or speak for a few minutes when awakening in the morning and reports perceptual disturbances upon awakening. After a thorough clinical interview, which of the following tests is an essential part of a work-up for this disorder?

The grandparent of a five-year-old child complains that their early morning sleep is disturbed by the child's loud play. Although the grandparent scolds the child, the behavior is getting worse. A psychiatrist advises the grandparent to praise the child frequently during quiet play and to consistently ignore any loud play. The psychiatrist hypothesizes that the grandparent's scolding is serving which of the following functions for the child?
Which of the following childhood mental health conditions is associated with the greatest risk for developing alcohol use disorder as an adult?
According to self-psychology, which of the following is considered typical in children?
Which of the following therapeutic modalities is based on the premise that the autonomic nervous system can come under voluntary control through operant conditioning?
What is the proposed mechanism of action by which omega-3 fatty acids exert their antidepressant activity?

An adolescent is having difficulty making friends, struggles with initiating conversations, exhibits poor eye contact, and has difficulty understanding social cues. The adolescent becomes easily upset with unexpected transitions and is very "rules focused." The patient prefers to be alone and spends considerable time reading about and discussing the solar system. The most likely diagnosis is:
A school-age child has a history of seizures, language regression, and hyperactivity. An electroencephalography is obtained and most likely will demonstrate which of the following findings?

options.text: Occipital spikes attenuated by eye opening
Intermittent brief generalized 4 Hz spike-and-wave bursts

stem: In addition to gender-affirming psychotherapy and appropriate social supports, what is the initial medical intervention for a patient who meets criteria for gender dysphoria with Tanner 2 stage puberty?
After an argument a child exclaims, "Nobody wants to be my friend anymore!" Which of the following cognitive errors is the child exhibiting according to cognitive behavioral theory?

options.text: Attending to negative features of events

stem: What is the primary goal of family therapy for oppositional defiant disorder?

options.text: Allowing the therapist to set limits with the child
Monitoring for signs of abuse to ensure the child's safety
Establishing a warm and mutually respectful relationship between parents and child
Providing psychoeducation to the parents about features of oppositional defiant disorder
Determining whether the family system has diffused or rigid boundaries with external systems

stem: An adolescent presents to the psychiatrist as a follow-up after starting an antipsychotic medication. During the evaluation, the adolescent is noted to have difficulty staying seated and endorses a new onset sense of restlessness. Which of the following is a first-line treatment of these symptoms?

A 30-month-old stacks blocks and sits next to a child of the same age who plays with a toy car. The caregiver facilitates play by exchanging toys between the two children. The caregiver is concerned as the 30-month-old does not share their toys directly with the other child and is more focused on showing their blocks to the caregiver. Which of the following is the best response to the caregiver's concern?

options.text: "The child is engaging in parallel play, which is normal for their age."
"The child needs more direction with their play due to inattention."
"The child is showing differential cooperation due to separation anxiety."
"The child is showing signs of autism and would benefit from evaluation."
"The child has evidence of poor attachment and would benefit from parent-child therapy."

stem: A medical student interviews a depressed adolescent patient, and then presents the history and exam to the resident. The resident notices that the student failed to ask about mania. What should the resident say first using the One Minute Preceptor Model of Teaching?

options.text: "What is your DSM diagnosis of this patient?"
"What is the most important rule-out for this case?"
"That was a great presentation. One thing you missed was\..."
"Did you ask about any history of elevated mood and energy?"
"How well do you think your interview and presentation went?"

stem: A 13-year-old patient is evaluated for escalating oppositional behaviors, including school truancy, running away from home, and substance use. The patient is given a provisional diagnosis of conduct disorder. The patient's parents ask if their child is likely to become a "lifetime criminal." Which of the following would be the most appropriate response regarding the course of conduct disorder?

options.text: "We do not currently have enough data to say."
"Most children are likely to become incarcerated as adults."
"Most children end up improving significantly by young adulthood."
"Most children become symptom-free with medication management."
"Most children progressively decline in functioning before they get better."

stem: Among youth ages 5-12, which of the following is the most significant influence on emotional development?
Which of the following statements accurately describes a forensic child psychiatric evaluation, as opposed to a clinical evaluation?

options.text: The physician has a fiduciary duty to the patient.
The purpose of the evaluation is to relieve suffering.
There is an increased opportunity for therapeutic bias to occur.
The client is considered to be the court or other retaining agency.
A physician-patient relationship is established; and thus, the evaluation remains confidential.

options.text: Direct consultation by a psychiatrist in the school setting
Child psychiatrist working as a consultant in a pediatric clinic
Pediatric residents rotating through child psychiatry fellowship programs
Pediatrician consulting child psychiatrist by telephone or electronic means

options.text: Evaluate staff for grief and depression
Advise administrators on how to respond
Evaluate students for grief and depression

options.text: Genes are repressed after a period of activity.
Introns are selectively spliced into the genome.
Genes of either paternal or maternal origin are silenced.

stem: An adolescent is evaluated for persistent lack of friends and preoccupation with fantasies that he has superpowers. On exam, his speech is vague, and his affect is fearful. What additional finding would lend support to a diagnosis of schizotypal personality disorder?

options.text: Fear of being separated from parents
Social anxiety not reduced by familiarity

options.text: Presence of an intact snout reflex

The use of short-acting methylphenidate was associated with an increase in tics.
There is no association between new onset or worsening of tics and psychostimulant use.

Which of the following factors is the strongest predictor for suicide and suicide attempts?

options.text: a psychiatrist at the school site.

stem: Children with encopresis are most likely to have which of the following comorbid psychiatric disorders?
Which of the following statements best describes the impact of marijuana use on adolescents transitioning into adulthood as reported in data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth?

options.text: Infrequent users had the least number of sexual partners and relationships.
Heavy users were the most likely to live with their parents in their late twenties.
Compared to other significant users, early quitters were less likely to have children.

options.text: Placement in a highly ranked school system
Focus on quick assimilation into the local community

options.text: Ask the caregivers to leave the room
Transfer the child to inpatient psychiatry

options.text: The child has impaired motor skills.
The child has below average intelligence.
The child is attending a disadvantaged school.

options.text: Major depressive disorder predicts the development of problematic social media use.
Social media use has a dose-dependent relationship with the development of depression.
Positive experiences on social media are associated with improved depressive symptoms.
Negative experiences on social media are associated with worsened depressive symptoms.

(Select three.)
Which of the following laboratory findings might be elevated in patients with anorexia nervosa? (Select three.)

A child admitted to an inpatient psychiatric hospital is severely agitated and aggressive toward staff. The patient does not respond to de-escalation techniques and refuses oral medication. Physical restraints are initiated, and the patient receives an intramuscular medication. According to the Joint Commission regulations, which of the following procedures should be followed? (Select three.)

options.text: Staff must monitor the child continuously while the child is in restraints.
The child should be removed from the physical restraints as soon as the child is calm.
Oral antihistamine medication should be administered after being released from the restraints.

Immediately after the removal of the restraints, the child should be moved to a locked seclusion room.
After the removal of the restraints, the clinician should hold a debriefing discussion with the patient.
